messages:
liz (product): Heads-up — we need to lock acceptance criteria for the audit snapshot lifecycle before we schedule the customer‑gated rollout for BYOK/private tenants. Posting a compact proposal + rollout gate idea, please react with gaps or concerns.

sam (eng): quick q — by snapshot lifecycle you mean the export/evidence snapshots we hand to customers & legal? or also internal archival snapshots?

liz (product): both, but this thread focuses on customer-facing evidence exports + the lifecycle that determines TTL, searchability, and encryption when BYOK is enabled. Internal archival details can be follow-up.

rohit (security): key points from security POV: envelope encryption with customer CMK for exported blobs, immutability flag while legal hold active, no plaintext caching in any intermediate store, and audit trail for each decrypt operation.

maya (legal): must include: per-export provenance (who exported, when, what filters), tamper-evident manifest, and an API to place/remove legal holds. Also need explicit retention-exemption flow and an attestation we can send to courts.

victor (sre): ops constraints: snapshot jobs can be huge (100s GB). We need backpressure, multipart upload, staged GC, and a cost estimate for N-day retention at scale. Also metrics + alerting for stuck exports.

sam (eng): proposed "Acceptance test checklist" (minimal, each item must have an automated E2E test):
1) Create export snapshot for tenant with default encryption; verify manifest created and indexable.
2) Create export snapshot with BYOK (CMEK) — verify the exported blob is encrypted under customer key and cannot be decrypted without CMK.
3) Trigger legal hold on a snapshot; verify TTL prevented and attempt to GC fails with clear audit event.
4) Restore/ingest a snapshot into a staging workspace; confirm data integrity + policies applied.
5) Export package contains provenance + tamper manifest and a checksum that verifies after download.
6) Export job failure/retry semantics: partial uploads should resume; jobs >24h must surface to oncall.

liz (product): rollout gating suggestion: internal dogfood -> two pilot tenants (security/compliance customers) -> tenant feature-flagged beta (10% traffic) -> staged 50% -> full. Each gate requires green on acceptance tests + security sign-off + legal checklist.

rohit (security): add: key-rotation scenario test: rotate CMK, old snapshots must still be decryptable (via key metadata/escrow or rewrap flow) OR we document inability and require customer-side rotation policy. Need to pick one.

maya (legal): we cannot force customer to hand over keys. So product must support evidence export decryptable by customer or provide documented escrow handshake. Legal prefers an auditable escrow flow for subpoenas, with explicit customer consent.

sam (eng): technical note on escrow: we can implement an optional, auditable key-wrapping escrow that requires a legal request + customer ACK. Adds dev work + compliance review.

victor (sre): operational runbook outline request: how oncall triages stuck exports, how to revoke a snapshot (if legal), and cost page for retention tiers (7/30/90/365 days). We need SLOs for export success rate and median export duration buckets.

liz (product): here's a tiny example of the test API we'll validate in automation — invite comments: 

```
# create snapshot request (BYOK)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"tenant_id":"T-ACCT-99","range":"2025-01-01..2025-03-31","encryption":"CMEK","cmk_id":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd"}'

# check status
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports/T-ACCT-99/exports/exp_0001/status
```

sam (eng): +1 to that shape. We'll need an export manifest schema (fields: id, tenant_id, created_by, time_range, manifest_checksum, cmk_meta, legal_hold_flag, items_count). Add schema to the spec doc.

rohit (security): also capture `key_policy_version` & `key_rotation_meta` in cmk_meta. If we support escrow, add `escrow_state` with audit events.

maya (legal): acceptance criterion: we should be able to produce an "evidence packet" that contains manifest + signed attestation + audit trail for every export within 48h of request. That must be automated for pilot customers.

liz (product): next steps I propose:
- Sam: draft full acceptance test matrix (items above -> test cases) by EOD Friday.
- Rohit: write security appendix on CMK/escrow options + recommended default behavior by Tue.
- Victor: run estimates for storage delta at 7/30/90/365 retention and draft runbook skeleton by Tue.
- Maya: legal hold API text + evidence attestation language and required customer consent flows by Wed.

sam (eng): I'll also sketch the feature-flag gating we need so we can flip per-tenant and do the canary rollout.

victor (sre): can we also include a small acceptance metric: export median < X minutes for <10GB snapshots? we'll define thresholds in the matrix.

liz (product): yes — include latency buckets (<1GB, 1-10GB, >10GB). We'll pick thresholds before canary.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/export-worker v3.2 -> staging at 2026-04-02T09:32:00Z :rocket:

sam (eng): noted. I'll start the matrix and paste into the spec PR.

rohit (security): :thumbsup: will review the PR early.

maya (legal): thanks — tagging legal-review when ready.

liz (product): great — thanks all. If anyone sees a non-negotiable item we missed, drop it here.

sam (eng): one more edge-case: exports for customers in regulated regions (EU/UK) need region-local export endpoints or an affirm flow that data left-region — add to matrix.

liz (product): added — regional export endpoint requirement.

rohit (security): OK locking this for draft. I'll file a sec-req ticket for CMK-escrow discussion.

victor (sre): adding brief note: GC job must be idempotent, and we should support a soft-delete -> hard-delete window for safety.

maya (legal): :white_check_mark: sounds good from legal side pending the attestation wording.

liz (product): awesome. I'll open the PR with the acceptance matrix and rollout gate checklist in ~1hr.

sam (eng): :party:
